- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast > true by >5%) — apply downward correction if sentiment drops post-spike.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 10–14 day average is > forecast, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after sentiment peaks: if sentiment > 0.8 and forecast > true by >2%, cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- Avoid overconfidence in high sentiment: if sentiment > 0.8 and forecast > 75% of 30-day mean, reduce by 2–5%.
- Correct for sentiment-driven volatility: if sentiment > 0.7 and true outcome < 65% of forecast, apply downward bias of 1–3%.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in high sentiment cycles — reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment > 0.6.
